findings.issue: _EDITS_A_COMMENT matches a verb (update|fix|correct|...) followed within 40 characters by the noun comment/docstring, and only the text AFTER the noun is checked for a clause join. A resolution that changes code BECAUSE of a comment matches: 'Update the loop to match the docstring', 'Fix the retry bug noted in the comment'. Each is a single clause with no join after the noun, so _says_no_code_change returns True and _fix_task_args (the new elif at ~3918) makes the task gate-only and returns before the _fix_clauses tests.add clauses are written. A real behaviour fix loses its red-first discipline and its suite clause; that is the false-green direction. Only the negative twin 'Fix the comment and the loop' (bx12 P1-R3) is pinned; no case covers a verb + code object + comment noun.
findings.resolution: Require the comment/docstring noun to be the object of the edit: anchor it directly after the verb and an optional determiner/adjective (e.g. ^(?:update|reword|...)\s+(?:the|this|that|its|a)?\s*(?:\w+\s+)?(?:comments?|docstrings?)\b), or reject when a code-ish noun or 'to match|per|noted in|described in' sits between verb and noun. Add bx12 rows for 'Update the loop to match the docstring' and 'Fix the bug the comment describes' staying tdd.

findings.issue: Reusing gateBasis `phase-no-paths` for 'files were named, none is a suite' is accurate in effect (no suite path to point the spelling at, so the phase gate is used) but the plan's own vocabulary defines the word narrowly as 'a sibling records a spelling and this task named no file to point a gate at' (init.md:398, _manifest_vocab.py:176-179). It is also not in GATE_BASIS_ANSWERED, so the validator warns on every such task that the gate is 'a default rather than a choice' and says 'Narrow it to the paths this task names' (_manifest_phases.py:1824-1833). For this task the paths it names are exactly the non-suite files that must not be pointed at, so the advice points at the bug this task fixes. The task note explains the real reason, but the machine-readable word and the warning mislead a reader of the plan.
findings.resolution: Either add a distinct word (e.g. `files-no-suite`, adding to an open vocabulary is free) to GATE_BASIS and GATE_BASIS_ANSWERED so the wide gate is read as an answer, or keep phase-no-paths and amend init.md:398 and the validator wording to say 'or none of its files is a suite; name the suite with --tests-add'.

findings.issue: The comment still says `expectRedFirst` is derived as `audit-task._build_task` writes `mode == "tdd"`. The diff changes the derivation to _expects_red_first(mode, tests_add, fix_task) in two writers (_build_task and _locked_scope), so the sentence now states a rule the code no longer follows.
findings.resolution: Reword to point at `audit-task._expects_red_first`, the one rule both writers read.
